testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Friction inside a brake drum happens when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Push against the inside of the drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Friction happens when the brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: For a vehicle with air brakes, how should the air compressor drive belt be checked before each drive?
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor belt before each drive. The belt should be tight and in good condition.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work.
The distance between the brake pedal's resting position and the floor.
The amount of air pressure needed to stop a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work.
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the air lines to reach the brakes. This creates a delay of at least one-half second between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes beginning to work. Hydraulic brakes work instantly when you press the pedal.

questions.question: When spring brakes are activated on a vehicle with air brakes, you should never:
questions.explanation: Never push the brake pedal when spring brakes are activated. The combined force of the springs and air pressure could damage the brakes.

questions.question: While driving, spring brakes are held in place by:
questions.explanation: While driving, air pressure holds the spring brakes in place. When air pressure drops low enough, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: The air storage tanks:

options.text: Hold enough air for only one braking cycle.
Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor stops.
Do not hold air unless there is an emergency.
Hold enough air for more than 1,000 braking cycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor stops.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: Emergency brakes:
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must work by mechanical force.

questions.question: To check if a trailer has ABS, you can:

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors behind the brakes.
Look under the hood for an ABS sticker.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors behind the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires behind the brakes.

questions.question: An air compressor governor stops the compressor from pumping when the air tanks reach:
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping air when the tanks reach 125 psi. This is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: Air tanks usually hold enough compressed air for:

options.text: Only one stop before needing to be refilled.
Several stops before needing to be refilled.

questions.correctAnswerText: Several stops before needing to be refilled.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold enough compressed air for the brakes to be used several times.

questions.question: What happens if one air system in a dual air brake system has very low pressure?

options.text: No brakes will work at all.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There will be no noticeable effect.
Lights on the tractor will flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, if one air system has very low pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully. Stop your vehicle safely and have the air system repaired.

questions.question: How many feet does an air brake vehicle need to stop from 55 mph under good driving conditions?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes thinking time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph in good conditions needs about 450 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: When should a low air pressure warning signal turn on?

options.text: When tank pressure drops below 120 psi.
When tank pressure drops below 60 psi.
When tank pressure drops below 10 psi.
When tank pressure drops below 5 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When tank pressure drops below 60 psi.
questions.explanation: A low air pressure warning signal must turn on if air pressure in the tanks drops below 60 psi. The warning may be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: Where are braking mechanisms located in a brake drum?
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels and located on the axles. The braking mechanisms that stop the vehicle are found inside the drum brake.

questions.question: What can happen if you use parking brakes in wet, freezing weather?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and lock the vehicle in place.
The brakes may suddenly release on their own.
The brakes may become too slippery to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and lock the vehicle in place.
questions.explanation: Do not use parking brakes in wet, freezing weather. The brakes could freeze and make it impossible to move the vehicle.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in an S-cam brake system, air pressure moves which part?
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal in an S-cam brake system, air enters the brake chambers. The air pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: What color is the ABS malfunction lamp?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow malfunction lamps.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air tank drains?

options.text: They allow rain water to enter the tanks.
They remove water and oil from the air tanks.
They must stay open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air usually contains water and compressor oil. Water and oil can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. Open the air tank drains daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: To stop normally in a vehicle with air brakes, push the brake pedal down. The harder you push the pedal, the more air pressure is released.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how are the air tanks set up?

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own separate air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.
Brakes work on only one side of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own separate air tanks.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems. A dual system has two separate air brake systems connected to one set of brake controls. Each system has its own air tanks.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure activates an electric switch. What else happens?

options.text: The low pressure warning light turns on.
The low pressure warning light turns off.

questions.explanation: In air brake systems, pressing the brake pedal pushes air pressure into an electric switch. This switch turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, both systems share:
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system use one air compressor. If this compressor fails, both systems will not work.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: All air tanks must have:
questions.explanation: All air brake tanks must have drain valves. These valves remove oil and water that build up in the tanks. They can be operated by hand or automatically.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that moves air from the compressor to the tanks
A noise made by air brakes when used
A part in the braking unit that lets air move freely

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when air pressure in the tanks drops below 60 psi.
